title: Stage 2 — Pull
subtitle: Texas, the same site, the same weather. Your plan this time.
_note: Identical seed, ground and events to stage1_texas on purpose (decided). Only plan, permits, preparation and the authored deviations differ.

crews.name: Backfill
crews._note: Default is the PM's Day 5; the team moves it in the huddle. Reference: Day 12 gives zero idle with no events (finish 35.0).

plan._note: Same contract as Stage 1 so the overlay compares like with like.

permits._openZoneLimit_validate: zones open to excavation and not yet backfilled and signed; stands in for the city's open-trench limit

checklist: Compaction test passed (result in Plan's inbox)

rules._permitFineUsd_validate: placeholder amount for pushing excavation past a permit boundary

defaultIndicator.wall: Stiff clay, vertical cut holding. Spoil pile set back about 2 ft.

indicator.wall: Clay softening toward the toe; a thumb goes in. Small slabs have let go near the bottom.
indicator.water: Water seeping from the lower wall; a puddle is forming along the toe.

card.title: Trench wall collapse at 7+20
facts: The lower wall has slumped into the pipe crew's working section.
Pipe crew is out of the trench.

cardWhenProtected.title: Wall movement at 7+20
facts: Clay has slumped against the trench box; the box held.
Pipe crew is out of the trench while the toe is cleaned up.

check.text: Read the plate on the excavator on site (Small, Standard, Large). Plan reads excavation's lead over pipe on the LOB; the lender loses the clearing days.
Budget: $18,000 now plus $150 a day for the rest of the job.
Lead days for this city on the Texas page, added to the clearing days. Plan checks the budget.

forecast.text: NWS: 70% chance of heavy rain tomorrow afternoon through the following day.

card.title: Heavy rain
facts: Every crew at half speed for two days.

options.label: Rent a drainage pump now

check.text: How many stations are open between the excavator and the backfill crew? Count the open-trench tokens; the rework is a day per 500 ft.

options._source: Workbook A2 option D: pump restores excavation and backfill to 100% during the rain, pipe laying unchanged; halving the rework is the new rule (accepted October 14, to validate)

events._source: Workbook A2: all crews at 50% for 2 days. Rework rule is new (accepted October 14, to validate).

deviations._note: If Plan buys a trench box for a stretch that does not cover 7+20, the box is placed exactly where Plan said. Only Site can see that it is in the wrong place.

The excavation foreman does not like idling at a boundary. The first time excavation reaches a zone without a posted permit, it digs 100 ft into it before stopping, unless Site is standing at the boundary or Plan has held the crew. The city fines it.

inbox.subject: Your plan
inbox.body: Same contract: promised finish Day 35, deadline Day 47, budget $278,400. The permits are yours to pull this time; the city allows two zones open. Buy what you can justify. I will be watching the daily report.

inbox.subject: Lead times this month
inbox.body: Excavators: Small 3 days, Standard 5, Large 7. Cranes: Standard 7, Heavy 10. Loaders: Small 3, Standard 5, Large 7. Mobilization $25,000 per order.

inbox.subject: Inspection calendar
inbox.body: Hold-point inspections available any day with a day's notice. Compaction results are returned the same evening.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Same site, same contract, your plan. You have thirty seconds before the trucks roll. The permits are in the spec-keeper's hands; two zones open at a time, the city says.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Same ground, two plans. Look at both sets of lines before anyone says which was better.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at seven-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.
